prompts.q: Which command shows free and used disk space per mounted filesystem?
prompts.note: -h prints sizes in human-readable units (GB/MB) instead of raw 1K blocks. “Disk is full — which mount?” → df. “What is eating this mount?” → du.

prompts.q: df -h shows plenty of free space, yet writes fail with "No space left on device". Which df flag reveals the likely cause?
prompts.note: Inode usage — a filesystem can run out of inodes with bytes to spare.

prompts.q: You want one human-readable size per item under /home, to spot the biggest. What do you run?
prompts.note: Canonical form here: -s (one summary line per argument) plus -h (human-readable). Pipe to `sort -rh` to rank largest-first.

prompts.q: Which du flag collapses output to one summary line per argument, instead of one line per subdirectory?
prompts.note: -h (human-readable sizes) is its usual companion: du -sh.

prompts.q: Which command lists all block devices and their partition layout as a tree?
prompts.note: `fdisk -l` also works but is heavier and needs root.

prompts.q: Which lsblk flag adds filesystem type, label, and UUID to the listing?
Which command, run with no arguments at all, lists every currently mounted filesystem and its options?
prompts.note: findmnt shows the same data as a tree.

prompts.q: Attach the partition /dev/sdb1 at the directory /mnt/data — what do you run?
prompts.note: Device first, mount point second. The directory must already exist; manual mounts vanish on reboot (persist them in /etc/fstab).

prompts.q: Which fdisk invocation inspects partition tables read-only, with no risk of modifying any disk?
prompts.note: Without -l, fdisk opens an interactive editor that can rewrite the partition table.

prompts.q: `fdisk /dev/sda` (no -l) does not just print the partition table — what does it open instead?
prompts.note: Single-letter commands queue changes, and 'w' writes them to disk immediately — only enter it when you mean to repartition.

prompts.q: Which command prints each partition's UUID and filesystem type (e.g. for writing /etc/fstab)?
In /etc/fstab, which identifier keeps mounting the right disk even when device names shift between boots?
prompts.note: Names like /dev/sdb1 depend on enumeration order at boot; the UUID is written into the filesystem at creation and never changes.

prompts.q: Which journalctl flag streams new log entries live, like `tail -f`?
Only SSH entries from the last hour: journalctl -u ssh {{--since}} "1 hour ago"
prompts.note: Takes human-friendly time expressions: "1 hour ago", "yesterday", "2026-01-01".

prompts.q: Which tail flag keeps the file open and prints new lines as they are appended, in real time?
prompts.note: Plain tail prints the last 10 lines and exits. -F additionally survives log rotation.

prompts.q: Show the last 100 lines, then keep streaming new ones: tail {{-n 100 -f}} file.log
A USB drive isn't being recognized. Which command shows kernel-level hardware messages that might explain why?
prompts.note: The kernel ring buffer logs hardware detection and driver events like USB attach/detach.

prompts.q: Which dmesg flag replaces seconds-since-boot with human-readable timestamps?
Inside less, how do you search forward for the text "failed"?
prompts.note: `?failed` searches backward; n / N repeat the search forward / backward.

prompts.q: Inside less, which key jumps to the end of the file (the newest log lines)?
prompts.note: Lowercase g jumps back to the top. `less +G file` opens already at the end.

prompts.q: Which tool rotates, compresses, and eventually deletes old log files so they never fill the disk?
prompts.note: Per-log rules live in /etc/logrotate.d/; a daily job runs them.

prompts.q: Which logrotate flag does a dry run — showing what would rotate without doing it?
prompts.note: Debug mode: prints the plan without touching any file.

prompts.q: Which command shows the recent login history — who logged in, from where, and when?
prompts.note: It reads /var/log/wtmp; `lastb` shows failed login attempts.

prompts.q: List the machine's recent reboots using `last` — what do you run?
prompts.note: The pseudo-user "reboot" filters the history to system reboots.

prompts.q: Using ps, snapshot every running process and filter to lines mentioning nginx — what is the classic pipeline?
prompts.note: pgrep -a nginx is the tidier purpose-built alternative.

prompts.q: In `ps aux`, which letter includes daemons — processes with no controlling terminal?
prompts.note: a = all users' processes, u = user-oriented columns (CPU/mem).

prompts.q: A server feels sluggish — which command gives a live, auto-updating view of the heaviest processes?
prompts.note: Unlike ps, top refreshes continuously.

prompts.q: Inside top, which key re-sorts the list by memory usage?
prompts.note: Shift+m. P sorts by CPU, k prompts for a PID to kill, q quits.

prompts.q: Which signal cannot be caught or ignored — the instant, no-cleanup kill?
prompts.note: Always try plain kill (SIGTERM) first; -9 can leave temp files, locks, or corrupt state behind.

prompts.q: Which signal does `kill 1234` send when no signal is specified?
prompts.note: The graceful request — the process may catch it and clean up before exiting.

prompts.q: How do you start a heavy backup job so it yields CPU to everything else?
prompts.note: Higher niceness = lower priority. renice changes it for an already-running process.

prompts.q: Which niceness value gives a process the lowest possible CPU priority?
prompts.note: The range is -20 (highest priority) to 19; only root may set negative values.

prompts.q: Which command prints just the PIDs of every running "python" process?
prompts.note: -a adds the full command line next to each PID.

prompts.q: Which command signals processes matched by name, instead of by PID?
prompts.note: pgrep's acting sibling — same matching rules, but sends SIGTERM (by default) instead of printing PIDs.

prompts.q: `umount /mnt/data` fails with "target is busy". How do you find which process is holding it open?
Which lsof invocation shows the process using TCP port 8080?
prompts.note: `ss -tulpn | grep 8080` is the socket-tool equivalent.

prompts.q: Which modern command shows a machine's IP addresses and network interfaces?
prompts.note: Short form: ip a. Successor to the older ifconfig.

prompts.q: View the routing table, including the default gateway — what do you run?
prompts.note: Short form: ip r. The "default via …" line is the gateway.

prompts.q: Which command (with flags) shows every listening port and the process that owns it?
prompts.note: t/u: TCP/UDP, l: listening, p: owning process, n: numeric ports.

prompts.q: ss replaces which older socket-inspection tool?
Which curl flag fetches only the HTTP response headers, not the body?
prompts.note: Long form --head. Fast way to check status, redirects, and server headers.

prompts.q: Print just the HTTP status code: curl -o /dev/null -s {{-w}} "%{http_code}" <url>
prompts.note: -w prints the format string after the transfer; -o /dev/null discards the body, -s silences progress.

prompts.q: Send exactly 4 pings, then stop: ping {{-c 4}} 8.8.8.8
prompts.note: Without -c, ping runs until Ctrl+C.
Echo request / echo reply — that's why ping can work when TCP services are down, and be blocked while they're up.

prompts.q: Requests to a remote server die somewhere along the path. Which command shows each router hop on the way?
Which traceroute flag skips reverse-DNS lookups so the hop list prints much faster?
A hostname resolves to the wrong address and you suspect DNS. Which command inspects its DNS records?
prompts.note: dig MX example.com queries a specific record type; @8.8.8.8 asks a specific nameserver.

prompts.q: Which dig option prints only the resolved values, omitting all query metadata?

prompts.note: Owner read+write, group and others read-only. Read=4, write=2, execute=1; each octal digit is one of owner/group/others.

prompts.q: Add execute permission to a script without changing any other bits — what do you run?
App files are owned by root but the www-data service account needs to write them. What is the correct fix?
prompts.note: Fix ownership — don't reach for chmod 777, which makes files world-writable.

prompts.q: Give alice ownership and set group devs in one command: chown {{alice:devs}} report.txt
prompts.note: user:group — one colon-joined argument sets both at once.

prompts.q: Which useradd flag ensures a home directory is created for the new user?
Which useradd flag sets the new account's login shell?
prompts.note: e.g. useradd -m -s /bin/bash alice

prompts.q: Disable a former contractor's login without deleting their account or files — what do you run?
prompts.note: -l locks the password so the account can't authenticate.

prompts.q: Re-enable a password-locked account — what do you run?
prompts.note: -u unlocks what -l locked.

prompts.q: Which sudo flag runs the command as a specific non-root user?
prompts.note: e.g. sudo -u postgres psql

prompts.q: What is the only safe way to edit /etc/sudoers (the file defining who may use sudo)?
prompts.note: It syntax-checks before saving — a broken sudoers can lock everyone out of root.

prompts.q: Add alice to the docker group without touching her other groups — what do you run?
prompts.note: She must log out and back in for it to apply.

prompts.q: After `usermod -G docker alice` (note: no -a), what happens to alice's other supplementary groups?
prompts.note: The classic footgun: without -a (append), -G replaces the entire supplementary group list.

prompts.q: Which command refreshes the local package index, and should usually run before `apt install`?
prompts.note: Otherwise install resolves against a stale index.

prompts.q: Which apt subcommand actually installs the newer versions of all installed packages?
prompts.note: update only refreshes the index; upgrade does the installing.

prompts.q: You downloaded a standalone .deb file. Which command installs it directly from disk?
prompts.note: apt normally installs from repositories; dpkg handles local files.

prompts.q: Find which installed package owns the file /usr/bin/curl — what do you run?
On a RHEL/Fedora server, what is the equivalent of Debian's `apt install`?
dnf is the successor to which older RHEL package tool?
What version of nginx would install, and from which repository — how do you check without installing?
Search available packages by keyword using the apt-cache tool — what do you run?
prompts.note: `apt search` is the friendlier front-end for the same query.

prompts.q: How do you list every package currently installed on a Debian/Ubuntu system?
prompts.note: dpkg -l is the lower-level equivalent.

prompts.q: Which command previews which packages have upgrades pending?
Which command cleans out packages that were pulled in as dependencies but are no longer needed?
Which apt subcommand uninstalls a package AND deletes its config files?
prompts.note: apt remove keeps the config files around for a future reinstall.

prompts.q: Search a whole directory tree for "TODO", showing file names and line numbers — what do you run?
prompts.note: -r recurses, -n adds line numbers, -i would ignore case.

prompts.q: Which grep flag inverts the match — printing lines that do NOT contain the pattern?
prompts.note: e.g. `grep -v "^#"` strips comment lines from a config file.

prompts.q: Delete logs untouched for over 30 days: find /var/log -name "*.log" {{-mtime +30}} -delete
prompts.note: +30 = modified more than 30 days ago. Run without -delete first to preview.

prompts.q: Find every file larger than 100 MB under / — what do you run?
Print just the first whitespace-separated field of every line in a log — what do you run?
In awk, which expression always refers to the LAST field of a line, whatever its position?
prompts.note: NF is the field count of the current line, so $NF is always the last field.

prompts.q: Write the substitution back into the file itself: sed {{-i}} 's/old/new/g' config.txt
prompts.note: s = substitute; the trailing g replaces every match on each line, not just the first.

prompts.q: Delete every line matching a pattern with sed — what do you run?
prompts.note: Add -i to apply it to the file rather than just printing the result.

prompts.q: find prints a list of files, but rm doesn't read filenames from stdin. Which command bridges them?
prompts.note: It turns stdin lines into command arguments: find ... | xargs rm

prompts.q: Which find/xargs flag pair delimits filenames with NUL bytes, so names with spaces survive?
prompts.note: find . -name "*.tmp" -print0 | xargs -0 rm

prompts.q: Extract just the usernames (field 1) from the colon-separated /etc/passwd — what do you run?
prompts.note: -d sets the delimiter, -f picks the field(s).

prompts.q: Fields split on one fixed character and nothing clever needed — which minimal tool slices them out?
prompts.note: Reach for awk instead when fields are whitespace-separated or you need logic.

prompts.q: Which command shows how much RAM and swap are currently in use?
In free's output, which column shows memory the kernel can actually give to new processes (reclaimable cache included)?
prompts.note: The "free" column alone looks alarmingly low on healthy systems — page cache counts as used.

prompts.q: The three load-average numbers from uptime cover which time windows?
On a 4-core machine, above which load average does work start queuing?
prompts.note: Load average counts runnable (and uninterruptible-IO) tasks — compare it to the core count, not to 1.0.

prompts.q: In `vmstat 2 5`, what are the 2 and the 5 (in order)?
prompts.note: A snapshot every 2 seconds, 5 times total.

prompts.q: Persistently high si/so columns in vmstat mean the system is doing what?
prompts.note: Swap-in / swap-out traffic — a sign of memory pressure.

prompts.q: You suspect a slowdown is disk-bound, not CPU-bound. Which command breaks down per-device disk I/O?
In iostat -x output, %util pinned near 100 means the device is what?
prompts.note: Requests arrive as fast as the device can service them.

prompts.q: Which command shows who is currently logged in AND what each of them is running?
w's header line shows the same load averages as which other command?
prompts.note: Per user, w also adds idle time and current command — the things plain `who` lacks.

prompts.q: Re-run `df -h` every 2 seconds and watch its output update in place — what do you run?
prompts.note: -n sets the refresh interval in seconds.

prompts.q: Which watch flag highlights the differences between successive refreshes?
Which tar flags extract a gzip-compressed archive?
prompts.note: Extract, gzip, verbose, file. -t instead of -x lists contents without extracting.

prompts.q: Create a gzip-compressed archive of /data: tar {{-czvf}} backup.tar.gz /data
prompts.note: Create, gzip, verbose, file — -f must come last, right before the archive name.

prompts.q: Which transfer mechanism makes rsync faster than scp on repeated syncs of the same directory?
prompts.note: Only the parts that changed since last time are sent over the wire.

prompts.q: Which rsync flag removes destination files that no longer exist in the source, making a true mirror?
prompts.note: Powerful but destructive: run with -n (dry run) first.

prompts.q: Copy a single config file to a remote server over SSH, one time — simplest tool and syntax?
Which scp flag copies a whole directory recursively?
Which gzip flag keeps the original file alongside the new .gz copy?
prompts.note: By default `gzip file.txt` replaces the file with file.txt.gz.

prompts.q: Decompress file.gz using the gzip binary itself — what do you run?
prompts.note: gunzip is the same thing; zcat / zless read the contents without decompressing on disk.

prompts.q: Download a release tarball in a script, saving it under a specific filename — what do you run?
A large download was interrupted. Which wget flag resumes it instead of restarting?
prompts.note: Mnemonic: continue.

prompts.q: Write an ISO image onto a USB stick at /dev/sdb — what do you run?
prompts.note: if= input file, of= output device, bs= block size, status=progress shows a live counter.

prompts.q: dd overwrites whatever of= names, with no confirmation. Which command do you run first to verify the target device?
prompts.note: A mistyped device name destroys a disk — check the device tree before every dd run.

prompts.q: Which systemctl verb makes a service start automatically at every boot (without starting it now)?
prompts.note: start runs it right now; they're independent. `enable --now` does both at once.

prompts.q: A service just failed. Which command shows its state plus its most recent log lines in one view?
Run backup.sh every day at 3:00 AM: {{0 3 * * *}} /opt/scripts/backup.sh
prompts.note: Minute 0 of hour 3, every day. Edit with crontab -e, list with crontab -l.

prompts.q: What are the five cron fields, in order?
A service failed to start. Which command shows just that service's recent journal entries?
Filter a unit's journal to error-priority-and-worse messages only — which flag and value do you add?
Cron jobs fire at odd times and you suspect the server's timezone. Which command shows time, timezone, and NTP state?
prompts.note: Fix it with timedatectl set-timezone <tz>.

prompts.q: Turn on NTP clock synchronization with timedatectl — what do you run?
Which scheduler runs a command exactly once at a future time, rather than on a recurring schedule?
prompts.note: echo "systemctl restart app" | at 02:00 — cron is for recurring jobs.

prompts.q: List the pending `at` jobs — what do you run?
Cancel pending `at` job number 3 — what do you run?
Boot feels slow. Which command ranks services by how long each took to start?
See the machine's total boot time, split into firmware/loader/kernel/userspace — what do you run?
prompts.note: No arguments needed; blame and critical-chain drill into the slow parts.

prompts.q: How many ways can a Finnish letter be pronounced?
prompts.note: Fully phonemic: every letter is always pronounced, always the same way — never silent, never context-dependent.

prompts.q: What is the technical term for a spelling system where one letter always equals one sound?
prompts.note: Finnish spelling is fully phonemic — if you can spell it, you can say it: kioski.

prompts.q: Which syllable of a Finnish word carries the stress?
prompts.note: Every word, no exceptions — even long loanwords.
First syllable, always.

prompts.q: How long is a doubled letter held, compared to a single one?
prompts.note: And length changes meaning: tuli (fire) vs tuuli (wind) vs tulli (customs).

prompts.q: tuli, tuuli, tulli — three different words. What single feature distinguishes them?
prompts.note: fire · wind · customs — short vs doubled (long) letters.

prompts.q: Which three letters are Finnish's front vowels?
prompts.note: They are independent letters, not accented a/o/u.

prompts.q: Which three letters are the back vowels?
prompts.note: e and i are neutral — they pair with either set.

prompts.q: Which rule says a native word's vowels must be all back or all front, never mixed?
prompts.note: e/i are neutral and go with either set: talossa (back) vs metsässä (front).
Front-vowel word (ä) takes the front form -ssä; back-vowel talo takes -ssa: talossa.
Every suffix that isn't neutral comes in a matched back/front pair.
syödä has front vowels (ö), so the question particle takes its front form -kö — compare Puhutko? (back).

prompts.q: How many syllables does a diphthong like uo occupy?
prompts.note: Both vowels glide together in a single syllable, pronounced exactly as written: suo (swamp), tie (road), yö (night).
diphthong ie

prompts.q: In consonant gradation, what are the two grades a stem alternates between?
prompts.note: Called KPT because it hits the stops k, p, t; the basic form is strong, most endings trigger the weak grade.

prompts.q: Which grade appears when an ending closes the syllable (like genitive -n)?
prompts.note: kauppa → kaupan

prompts.q: Which two endings keep the strong grade instead of weakening it?
prompts.note: Partitive -a/-ä and the illative don't close the preceding syllable the same way.

prompts.q: kk weakens to what in the weak grade?
prompts.note: kukka → kukan (flower)
kk → k in the weak grade (flower).

prompts.q: pp weakens to what in the weak grade?
prompts.note: kauppa → kaupan (shop)
pp → p — the canonical KPT example (shop).

prompts.q: tt weakens to what in the weak grade?
prompts.note: tyttö → tytön (girl)
tt → t in the weak grade (girl).

prompts.q: In the weak grade, what usually happens to a single k?
prompts.note: jalka → jalan (foot). After u/y it turns into v instead: puku → puvun.
k drops out entirely (foot).
k → v after u (suit).

prompts.q: After u or y, a weakening k becomes which consonant?
prompts.note: puku → puvun (suit); elsewhere it just disappears (jalka → jalan).
leipä → leivän (bread)
p → v (bread); front harmony (ä) keeps the ending -än.
katu → kadun (street); pöytä → pöydän (table)
t → d in the weak grade (street).
t → d (table); front harmony (ä).
Helsinki → Helsingin; kenkä → kengän (shoe)
nk → ng in the weak grade.
nk → ng (shoe); front harmony (ä).
ranta → rannan (shore)
ilta → illan (evening)
rt → rr (beard).
mp → mm (comb).

prompts.q: The s-cases (-ssa/-sta/-Vn) translate which three English prepositions?
prompts.note: Interior cases: talossa · talosta · taloon.

prompts.q: The l-cases (-lla/-lta/-lle) translate which three English prepositions?
prompts.note: Exterior (surface) cases: pöydällä · pöydältä · pöydälle.

prompts.q: talossa vs pöydällä — which one means 'on'?
prompts.note: l-cases = surface (on the table); s-cases = interior (talossa — in the house).
Inessive. talossa — in the house; Helsingissä — in Helsinki.
Two rules fire at once: KPT weakens pp→p, harmony picks -ssa (back vowels).
i-final nouns often shift i→e in the stem: Suomi → Suome- + -ssa.

prompts.q: Which case ending means 'out of / from inside'?
prompts.note: Elative. talosta — out of the house; Suomesta — from Finland.
Same i→e stem shift as the inessive.
pp→p (KPT) plus back harmony -sta.

prompts.q: What is the commonest shape of the illative ('into')?
prompts.note: talo → taloon; Helsinki → Helsinkiin
Illative keeps the strong grade (pp stays pp) — unlike -ssa/-sta.

prompts.q: talossa vs taloon — which one means 'into'?
prompts.note: Illative = motion toward the inside; inessive talossa = static 'in'.

prompts.q: Which case ending means 'on / at' (and also expresses 'have')?
prompts.note: Adessive. pöydällä — on the table; also Minulla on... — I have...
t→d (KPT) plus back harmony -lla.
t→d plus front harmony -llä.

prompts.q: Which case ending means 'off / from a surface'?
prompts.note: Ablative. pöydältä — off the table.
t→d plus front harmony -ltä.

prompts.q: Which case ending means 'onto / to' (a surface or person)?
prompts.note: Allative — note it doesn't harmonize (always -lle). pöydälle — onto the table.
t→d (KPT); -lle is invariant.

prompts.q: What grade does the nominative (dictionary) form always keep?
prompts.note: kauppa on iso — the shop is big.

prompts.q: Which case marks the subject of a Finnish sentence?
prompts.note: The bare form — also the form dictionaries list: kauppa on iso.
And the stem weakens to the weak grade: talon ovi — the house's door.
pp→p gradation strikes again in the genitive: kaupan ovi — the shop's door.
The signature Finnish case: Juon kahvia — I drink (some) coffee.
vesi is an e-stem: partitive is vettä, not 'vesiä'.

prompts.q: Which grade does the partitive keep?
prompts.note: Like the illative — it doesn't close the syllable the same way.

prompts.q: After the number 'kaksi' (two), what case does the noun take?
prompts.note: Not the plural: kaksi taloa — two houses. Applies to all numbers 2+.
Numbers 2+ take the partitive singular: kissa → kissaa.

prompts.q: What case does the object take in a negative sentence?
prompts.note: Juon kahvin (I'll drink the coffee) → En juo kahvia (I don't drink coffee).
Negative verb en + bare stem juo; object kahvi → partitive kahvia.

prompts.q: puhua: puhun, puhut, puhuu, puhu{{mme}}, puhu{{tte}}, puhu{{vat}}
prompts.note: One set of personal endings for every verb: -n -t – -mme -tte -vat; 3sg (puhuu) lengthens the vowel instead.

prompts.q: How does the 3rd person singular (hän) mark the verb, instead of adding an ending?
prompts.note: puhu- → puhuu

prompts.q: Which part of the sentence makes the pronouns minä/sinä optional?
prompts.note: puhun already means 'I speak' — the -n carries the person, no minä needed.

prompts.q: olla (to be) — the minä form ('I am')?
prompts.note: Full irregular paradigm: olen, olet, on, olemme, olette, ovat.
olla is irregular — memorize the full paradigm.

prompts.q: olla (to be) — the hän form ('he/she is')?
prompts.note: Hän on opettaja — he/she is a teacher.

prompts.q: Type 1 verbs (like puhua) — how do you find the stem?
prompts.note: puhua → puhu-, then add endings: puhun
Type 1: drop -a → sano-, add -n.

prompts.q: Type 2 verbs (like syödä) — how do you find the stem?
prompts.note: syödä → syö-, then add endings: syön
Type 2: drop -da → juo-, add -n.

prompts.q: Type 3 verbs (like tulla) — how do you find the stem?
prompts.note: tulla → tul- → tule-, then add endings: tulen
Type 3: menn- → men- + -e- → mene-, add -n.
Type 3: opiskell- → opiskel- + -e- → opiskele-, add -n.

prompts.q: Type 4 verbs (like haluta) — how do you find the stem?
prompts.note: haluta → halua-, then add endings: haluan
Type 4: haluta → halua- + -n.

prompts.q: In a negative sentence, what form does the main verb take?
prompts.note: The negative word itself conjugates: en/et/ei/emme/ette/eivät. puhun → en puhu.
ei is the 3sg negative form; syö is the bare stem.

prompts.q: Which negative verb form goes with minä ('I don't')?
prompts.note: The negative word conjugates like a verb: en, et, ei, emme, ette, eivät.

prompts.q: How do you form a yes/no question in Finnish?
prompts.note: Puhutko suomea? — Do you speak Finnish?
on + -ko → Onko; back harmony.

prompts.q: Which single pronoun covers both 'he' and 'she'?
prompts.note: Finnish has no grammatical gender — one pronoun does both.

prompts.q: How many articles (a/an/the) does Finnish have?
prompts.note: Definiteness comes from context and word order: Hän on opettaja — he/she is a teacher.

prompts.q: How does Finnish express 'to have' without a verb for it?
prompts.note: Literally 'on me is': Minulla on koira — I have a dog.
minulla = on me (adessive of minä).

prompts.q: Finnish has no future tense — what expresses future time instead?
prompts.note: Huomenna menen kauppaan — tomorrow I'll go to the shop.

prompts.q: Say: 'Tomorrow I go to the shop.' (as Finnish would say it)
prompts.note: No future tense needed — huomenna (tomorrow) does the work.

prompts.q: What language family does Finnish belong to?
prompts.note: A completely separate tree from English, Hindi, Russian, French (all Indo-European).

prompts.q: English, Hindi, Russian and French all belong to which family — the one Finnish is NOT part of?
